stemMd: Which statement must be true in every permitted order?

options.label: B
options.textMd: Ada must not be in position 1.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Ciro and Enzo must occupy consecutive positions, in either order.

explanationMd:
Combine the ordering and placement constraints rather than assuming one example is unique. The statement "Ciro and Enzo must occupy consecutive positions, in either order." holds in all 4 permitted orders. Generate the cases by placing any fixed-position item and adjacent block first, then discard arrangements that violate a remaining rule. For each alternative, an explicit permitted counterexample appears in its feedback.

Complete permitted orders (each arrow advances one position):
- Ada → Bela → Dina → Ciro → Enzo
- Ada → Ciro → Enzo → Bela → Dina
- Bela → Dina → Ciro → Enzo → Ada
- Ciro → Enzo → Bela → Dina → Ada

distractorRationale.b: A counterexample satisfying all the rules is Ada → Bela → Dina → Ciro → Enzo. Thus this statement is not necessary.
distractorRationale.a: A counterexample satisfying all the rules is Ada → Bela → Dina → Ciro → Enzo. Thus this statement is not necessary.
distractorRationale.d: A counterexample satisfying all the rules is Bela → Dina → Ciro → Enzo → Ada. Thus this statement is not necessary.

Rules Ada must occupy position 1 or position 5. Bela must precede Dina. Ciro must precede Enzo. Bela and Ciro must not occupy consecutive positions. leave 4 valid orders: Ada>Bela>Dina>Ciro>Enzo; Ada>Ciro>Enzo>Bela>Dina; Bela>Dina>Ciro>Enzo>Ada; Ciro>Enzo>Bela>Dina>Ada. Choice true counts: a=2, b=2, c=4, d=2; necessary requires all matches.
